grafias_do_espelho: PER YEAR: $40–150 MILLION IN LOST BENEFITS · CANADIAN ENTITY
Source: Congressional Research Service, 2024; U.S. Public Law 118-272
texto_aprovado: The alternative has a price too. The American agencies that run the treaty once estimated that a call on Canada would cost between 4 and 34 million dollars per request. British Columbia's estimate is that relying on those calls would cost the United States 40 to 150 million dollars a year in lost power. Beside the American figure, which is per call, 37.6 million a year looks steep. Beside the Canadian one, which is per year, it looks cheap.

divergencias: O estudo da BC (BC Ministry of Energy and Mines, 25/06/2013, p. 11; lido hoje no original) diz: 'BC Hydro analysis estimated U.S. energy losses due to effective use at these facilities (in a Called Upon year) to be approximately 1,300-3,000 gigawatt hours with an estimated value of $40 to $150 million.' É o valor num ano em que o Canadá é chamado, não um custo de todo ano. O CRS (nota 40) resumiu como 'per year', e a voz segue o CRS: 'would cost the United States 40 to 150 million dollars a year' e 'Beside the Canadian one, which is per year, it looks cheap'. A voz está gravada; a tela não deve dizer mais que o original ('PER YEAR' sozinho). A comparação 'per call × per year' perde força: as duas cifras são por evento. Quem decide é o Lucas
Detalhe de dono: a cifra é 'BC Hydro analysis' num documento do governo da província; 'CANADIAN ENTITY' (a BC Hydro, nota 2 do CRS) está certo
